naming_notes.mathers: Suits: Sceptres (= wands; Mathers: 'Wands, Sceptres, or Clubs'), Cups, Swords, Pentacles ('Deniers / Money, Circles, or Pentacles'). Courts: King, Queen, Knight, Knave (-> page); 'Deuce' -> two. Trumps numbered 1-21 plus 0: 1 The Juggler (-> the-magician), 5 The Hierophant or Pope, 8 Themis, or Justice (-> justice), 11 Strength, or Fortitude (-> strength), 12 The Hanged Man (-> the-hanged-one), 16 The Lightning-struck Tower (-> the-tower), 20 The Last Judgment (-> judgement), 0 The Foolish Man (-> the-fool, listed between 20 and 21), 21 The Universe (-> the-world). Minors numbered 22-77, King-to-Ace order per suit. 'number_in_source' and 'name_in_source' kept per entry.
naming_notes.papus: Third Lesson numbers trumps 1-22: 1 The Juggler (-> the-magician), 5 The Pope (-> the-hierophant), 8 Justice, 11 Strength, 12 The Hanged Man (-> the-hanged-one), 16 The Lightning-struck Tower, 17 The Stars (-> the-star), 20 The Judgment (-> judgement), 21 The Foolish Man (-> the-fool), 22 The Universe (-> the-world). Papus's suits elsewhere in the book: Sceptres, Cups, Swords, Pentacles (also 'Money'); courts King, Queen, Knight (also 'Cavaliers'), Knave.
naming_notes.westcott: Letter spellings normalised to: Aleph, Mem, Shin, Beth, Gimel, Daleth, Kaph, Pe, Resh, Tau, Heh, Vau, Zain, Cheth, Teth, Yod, Lamed, Nun, Samech, Oin (=Ayin), Tzaddi, Qoph. Values are quoted in Westcott's wording ('Capricornus', 'Sexual desire', 'Seventh Day of the week'). Extra fields: 'notes' and 'direction_positional' (a positional pairing, NOT an allotment stated by the text).

problems: Westcott edition: sacred-texts.com (labelled 1887) is behind a Cloudflare block (HTTP 403/5xx) and was not read. The 1887 1st edition was not found in public-domain scan form. Values come from the 1893 2nd edition (archive.org Google scan + Wikisource proofread transcription of the same edition). The 1911 3rd-ed. text was only cross-checked via a 1996 copyrighted reprint (Kuntz); in that reprint the main text of Ch. III-V matches 1893 almost word for word, but the two 'Supplement' sections (the source of every per-letter planet/day/gate/sign/month/organ/function value) do not appear. I could not establish from a primary scan whether Westcott himself dropped them in 1911 or whether Kuntz did.

Translation vs notes, and main text vs supplement: Westcott's main text (Ch. IV-V) only LISTS planets, days, gates, qualities, directions, signs, months and organs; it does not pair them letter by letter. The per-letter allotments are in the Supplements, which Westcott calls 'a modern illustration ... not found in the ancient copies' (from Kalisch). Note 40 says the planet allotment of both Kircher (Beth-Sun, Gimel-Venus, Daleth-Mercury, Kaph-Luna, Peh-Saturn, Resh-Jupiter, Tau-Mars) and Kalisch's supplement are 'wrong', and that 'the true attribution is however, not anywhere printed'. The 1911 wording (per reprint) is 'according to clairvoyant investigation' and 'probably not anywhere printed'.

Directions: no letter-by-letter direction is given for doubles (Ch. IV.2 lists Above, Below, East, West, North, South, Palace of Holiness) or simples (Ch. V.1 lists twelve directions). 'direction' is null for all 22. 'direction_positional' pairs list order with letter order only as an editor aid. Positional pairing is unreliable: the same positional reading of the Ch. V.1 property list (Sight, Hearing, Smell, Speech...) contradicts the supplement (Heh=Speech, Cheth=Sight...).

Double-letter opposites: Ch. IV.1 gives qualities Life, Peace, Wisdom, Riches, Grace, Fertility, Power and pairs Life/Death, Peace/War (Evil), Wisdom/Folly, Riches/Poverty, Grace/Indignation, Fertility/Solitude (Desolation), Power/Servitude, without assigning them to letters. The supplement assigns single qualities (Beth Wisdom, Gimel Health, Daleth Fertility, Kaph Life, Pe Power, Resh Peace, Tau Beauty). Opposites were filled by matching these; Gimel (Health) and Tau (Beauty) have no matching pair, so they are null, and Riches/Poverty and Grace/Indignation stay unassigned. Note 42 gives the Latin pairs of Postellus and Pistorius.

Simple-letter twelve properties: the supplement gives Vau 'mind' where the main text's list has 'Imagination' (note 44: Postellus 'suspicion', Pistorius 'mind'). Organs: the main-text list includes 'gall' but the supplement gives Tzaddi 'gullet', and Lamed 'private parts' with the remark '(Kalisch gives "gall.")'. Note 47 says the organ list varies between versions.

Tzaddi month: the supplement text (both the 1893 scan and Wikisource) reads 'formed with it Aquarius in the Year, and the gullet in Man'. No month is named, so month is null. ('Sabat' is 11th in the main-text month list.)

Westcott note 45 (the zodiac 'signs' Teth, Shin, Tau...) gives the Hebrew initials of the sign names (Teth=Taleh=Aries, etc.). These are NOT the simple letters and were not used for letter-sign values.

Westcott Ch. III mothers: the text gives Shin/Fire heavens-heat-head, Mem/Water earth-cold-belly, Aleph/Air air-temperate-chest. 'Season' records what the text says (heat/cold/temperate state of the Year). Westcott names no actual seasons.

Mathers: values come from the sacred-texts.com HTML transcription (via Wayback; the live site is blocked), not a page scan. Its typos are kept verbatim, e.g. Ace of Sceptres 'Pursuits Voilence' (sic, probably 'Pursuit, Violence'), 'the to the inexperienced'. Several entries lack commas ('Undertaking Movement', 'Mercy, Beneficence Kindness', 'Trials Surmounted'). Verify against a 1888 scan before quoting. Gutenberg (down for maintenance) and the Global Grey PDF (removed, 404) were unavailable.

Mathers: Five of Swords reversed reads 'Losses Trouble (same signification, whether reversed or not.)'; The Devil is just 'Fatality for Good' / 'Fatality for Evil'. Mathers also gives an Etteilla-derived 'additional remarks' list for 20 cards (combinations and reversals). That list is not included in the JSON.
Mathers: for the Hierophant and Justice entries the separator is '. ' not '.--'. The Six of Pentacles uses ':' before 'R.'. Parsing handled both. Split on the first '; R.' only.

Papus: used the 1892 1st English edition (Cornell scan), not the 1910 2nd edition (the Wellcome 1910 copy is marked in copyright, so it was not read). Papus gives only keywords and no reversed meanings. The trump meanings 7-22 are printed in two columns, and the OCR separates names from values. Pairing was rebuilt from column order (16 names, 16 values) and should be verified against the page image (p. 317). OCR errors were silently corrected: 'EcoNOMr'->'Economy', 'EuiN'->'Ruin', 'Mad- ness'->'Madness', 'Providential Pro- tection'->'Providential Protection'. Papus's Third Lesson also states that the first seven trumps chiefly refer to the intellectual side, the next seven to the moral side, and the last seven to material life.
Papus Sixth Lesson (Etteila's method) and the Second Lesson give minor-arcana meanings. These were out of scope and not extracted.
Public-domain status: Mathers 1888, Papus/Morton 1892 and Westcott 1893 are public domain. The 1996 Kuntz reprint is copyrighted and was used only as a cross-check; no values were taken from it.
